tools.name: proof_fetch_preflight
tools.description: Free: checks a public URL and returns fetchability, provenance, hashes, deterministic injection indicators and a free preview of the first 1,000 or so characters of text (short pages come back whole); not a safety guarantee. No payment or purchase. Example: {"url":"https://example.com/","maxChars":3

tools.name: proof_fetch_offer
tools.description: Returns the offer ($0.01 a page with a 500-page card pack, or $0.50 per call through Stripe MPP) and request schema without buying. Paid cited text uses POST /v1/evidence with Stripe MPP and a caller-generated idempotency key. Example arguments: {}.

tools.name: proof_fetch_evidence
tools.description: Paid: fetch a public URL and return its cited, paragraph-addressable text with integrity hashes and a receipt. Uses one prepaid credit, and only when extraction succeeds. Needs a ProofFetch key sent as the MCP request header Authorization: Bearer <key> (sold on the ProofFetch home page). Example: {"

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "proof_fetch_evidence" references sensitive artifacts (authorization, bearer). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: proof_fetch_preflight, proof_fetch_offer, proof_fetch_evidence · Public sink: proof_fetch_offer.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: proof_fetch_preflight, proof_fetch_offer, proof_fetch_evidence · Public sink: proof_fetch_offer

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "proof_fetch_preflight" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
